tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir/OTP engineer finishing Cornerman's port of the `run` command of Ringer (a Python agent-swarm CLI). The previous round's implementation passed the full suite on macOS and Linux; a code review cleared it to land after a short list of fixes. Your job is those fixes. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo at trunk. Edit files here directly.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the conformance tests are the acceptance check), DIVERGENCES.toml, bin/, mix.exs, mix.lock, vendor/, .git. Do not git commit, push or git add. Add no dependencies.

OWNED PATHS: anything under lib/cornerman/, plus ./notes.md.

STEP 1: START FROM THE PREVIOUS ROUND. Apply /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/out/fixup2-claude-sonnet/phase2a.patch with `git apply` (made against 517ad3e; only test/, DIVERGENCES.toml and swarms/ changed on trunk since). Its author's notes: /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/out/fixup2-claude-sonnet/notes.md. Keep its design, including the perl wrapper that makes a command "done" only at exit plus stdout EOF.

STEP 2: THE REVIEW. Read /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/review-fixup2-sonnet.md. Fix, with the conformance cases that now pin them (red on the previous round):
1. Perl settings in the caller's environment must not steer the wrapper (run/worker-environment-perl-vars: PERL_UNICODE=SDA, PERL5OPT=-Mwarnings=FATAL,all, PERL5LIB=/nonexistent). Isolate the wrapper completely: run perl with an environment scrubbed of every PERL* variable, PERLIO and the locale variables, pass the command's full, unchanged environment to it separately, and have the wrapper exec the command with exactly that environment. Also set PERL_BADLANG=0 for the wrapper only (finding 6), prefer /usr/bin/perl with PATH as a fallback (finding 8), and delete resolve/1 (finding 7: perl's exec searches the command's own PATH).
2. A wedged Spawn.Run must never hang its task (test/cornerman/spawn_exec_crash_test.exs: kill erlexec's :exec server under a running command; the caller must still get exactly one {:exit, _}, the command's group must die, and later spawns must work once erlexec restarts :exec). Accept any leader EXIT reason.
3. A command that cannot be exec'd (run/worker-exec-fails: an executable script whose interpreter does not exist) is what Ringer calls a spawn failure: one ERROR attempt, no retry, the eval notes carry `worker_error=<message>` and the worker log `[ringer.py] worker spawn failed: <message>\n`, where <message> is Python's OSError text, e.g. `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<path>'` (ringer.py _run_worker 9189-9201; Cornerman.Py has an os_error helper). The wrapper must report an exec failure distinctly from the command's own exit 127.
4. After a timeout, the reported worker status is the command's own status if it had already exited (run/timeout-reports-the-exited-workers-status: the worker exits 0, a SIGTERM-ignoring child forces the timeout, Ringer logs `attempt 1 exited rc=0`). The wrapper knows the status as soon as it reaps the command; get it to Spawn.Run before any SIGKILL can take the wrapper (a side channel separate from the command's output). Keep killing the whole group on timeout: Ringer's failure to SIGKILL there is a Ringer bug, recorded in DIVERGENCES.toml.
5. Suppress task-crash reports narrowly instead of setting Logger to :none for the whole run (finding 5): a crashing lifecycle stops with {:shutdown, reason} so neither the gen_statem nor its supervisor logs it, and run/task-crash's stderr stays exactly the `cornerman: error:` line. Other log output (for example erlexec's own errors) must reach stderr again.
6. The smaller items in finding 9: reset SIGFPE (and any signal the wrapper inherited as ignored) to its default before the wrapper re-raises a command's death signal; invalid UTF-8 in argv must not crash the wrapper's argument encoding.
Leave finding 4 (erlexec's 64 KB argv limit) alone; it becomes its own issue. Say in notes.md if you see a cheap guard.

DESIGN RULES: the run subtree stays host-agnostic (no System.halt, no terminal writes except through the sink); tasks are :gen_statem, restart :temporary, retries explicit transitions; OS processes only through Cornerman.Spawn; data-plane strings byte-identical to Ringer.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages and this worktree has no submodule checkout):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1 CORNERMAN_ORACLE=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py CORNERMAN_PYTHON=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test                                               # everything. Must pass in full.
  mix test test/conformance/run_test.exs:<line>          # one case
  mix test test/cornerman/spawn_exec_crash_test.exs
In this sandbox `ps` is blocked, so spawn tests that check liveness with `ps` can misreport; say so in notes.md rather than working around it. The verifying check (60 s limit) runs a smoke subset outside your sandbox; the orchestrator then runs the whole suite twice on macOS and Linux, so make `mix test` pass in full yourself before you stop.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the change under lib/cornerman/, formatted, compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md with: what you changed for each numbered item and how you verified it, the final `mix test` result line, anything your sandboxed run could not exercise, and any conformance case you believe is wrong, with the reason.
tasks.verified: the review's pre-landing fixes hold: perl settings can't steer the wrapper, a dead :exec server can't hang a task, exec failures are Ringer's spawn failures, an exited worker's status survives a timeout; a spread of run and lint cases match the oracle.
